ledger.claim: The deviation is established on the platform's own recorded distances, as POL-RD-22 requires: the recommended route was 11.8 km and the vehicle was driven 13.1 km, a deviation of 1.30 km. That is 0.30 km beyond the 1.0 km tolerance, so the within-tolerance rows of the refund matrix cannot apply and the deviation is a real one.

The driver-device trace is used only for what POL-RD-22 permits it to show - which route was taken and when - and it shows the vehicle leaving the recommended route at the PIE / Adam Road exit at 17:04:15 and not rejoining until Bishan Road / Braddell Road at 17:16:09: nearly twelve minutes driven on the Adam Road-Thomson Road line while the recommended route ran PIE, CTE, Braddell Road. This was a sustained departure, not a kerbside manoeuvre.

POL-RD-23 is not satisfied, so the reroute was not traffic-justified. The only traffic data on file is the LTA advisory for precisely this segment - PIE, Adam Road to CTE interchange, towards Changi - and the retrieved window (16:22:25 to 17:52:25) covers the trip. It reports type NONE: 'No incident, roadwork or closure recorded for the queried segment and window. Speed bands 4-5 throughout.' No congestion, incident or closure is recorded on the recommended route, and POL-RD-23 says in terms that a driver's assertion of traffic with no such data does not justify the reroute. The driver's 'PIE was slow' is therefore an unsupported assertion.

Row (d) of the refund matrix governs: the reroute was not traffic-justified and the deviation exceeds 1 km, so the excess distance fare is refunded in full. That fare is the deviation distance times the base per-km rate, without surge: 1.30 km x 0.72 SGD = 0.94 SGD, which is the figure the fare ledger itself derives. The rider's round 3.00 SGD figure is not the measure POL-RD-24 provides; the 0.94 SGD excess is the sum the matrix owes and it must be returned to the rider.

The driver's account that he 'messaged the passenger and she said ok' cannot move this case into a no-refund row. Every no-refund row of POL-RD-24 - (a), (b) and (c) - requires the reroute to be traffic-justified, and that condition fails on the LTA data. Row (d), which governs, contains no notification element at all, so the refund follows whether or not the rider was told or agreed.

In any event the asserted notice and the rider's alleged agreement are not established. The chat artifact is IMPAIRED - issue code TRUNCATED_LOG, weight_multiplier 0.6 - carrying only 2 of the 4 entries that trip_record.chat_message_count records, and both entries it does carry are timestamped before the trip started (16:50:25 and 16:50:55) and say nothing about any deviation; the trip record's own messages_during_trip block is empty. Under POL-RD-21 the notice obligation is the driver's to prove - with in-app chat, or a call recording, and this record carries no in-app calls at all - and on an impaired, truncated log it is not proved.

This is a case the AI should decide and finish, not hand up. Neither profile carries a fraud flag (rider_profile.fraud_flags 0, driver_profile.fraud_flags 0), so POL-GEN-22's 0.95 uplift does not apply, and at 3.00 SGD the dispute sits below the 10.00 SGD band where the AI ruling is final at any confidence. The deviation of 1.30 km is within POL-RD-25's 2 km limit for an AI ruling, and the record carries no safety indicator that would force human review under POL-GEN-21.

Escalation would help no one here and would hurt the rider: under POL-GEN-03 an escalated case issues no monetary outcome and the amount is simply held, which leaves the rider carrying the disputed charge on a question the record fully answers. Because the deviation is measured (1.30 km), the justification is tested and absent (LTA type NONE), and the remedy is fixed by the matrix (0.94 SGD), there is no fact of POL-RD-24 left open to escalate under POL-GEN-26.

The present state is that the rider bears the whole of it: the ledger shows the metered fare of 17.81 SGD charged (payment_status CHARGED) with refund_issued_sgd 0.00. Nothing has yet been given back, so PARTIAL_REFUND of the excess distance fare is the ruling that stops the rider carrying the disputed excess, and it is the relief the rider's claim, read against the policy, actually supports.

The deviation is fixed by the platform's own recorded distances at 1.30 km (13.1 km actual less 11.8 km recommended, POL-RD-22), and the only money POL-RD-24 moves for a non-justified deviation over tolerance is the excess distance fare: 1.30 km x 0.72 SGD/km = 0.94 SGD, per row (d). The rider's demand for 3.00 SGD exceeds the policy figure by 2.06 SGD, and that excess must be refused; NO_ACTION as to the balance.

FULL_REFUND is reserved for a filing party who is entirely right (POL-GEN-03), and the rider is not: the remedy for this deviation is measured in distance, not in the rider's round 3.00 SGD estimate. The rider is owed at most the 0.94 SGD excess distance fare; the remainder of the contested amount is not supported by any clause and the present charge stands as to it.

The LTA advisory for the PIE / Adam Road to CTE segment across the trip window records type NONE, speed bands 4-5 throughout and no incident, roadwork or closure, so the driver's assertion that the PIE was slow cannot carry a traffic justification under POL-RD-23. The operative row is therefore POL-RD-24(d): refund of the excess distance fare in full and nothing beyond it.

The chat log is IMPAIRED - weight_multiplier 0.6, issue code TRUNCATED_LOG, only 2 of the trip's 4 messages exported and nothing after pickup - so it cannot establish that the driver deviated without a word. The driver's statement on file, that he messaged the passenger about the slow PIE and she said ok, is not contradicted by the impaired export, and the rider bears the burden of showing the deviation was unexplained.

Neither party's history decides this trip: POL-GEN-01 makes prior disputes, ratings, account age and deviation flags context only, and the one profile field that could raise the confidence an AI ruling needs - fraud_flags - is 0 on both the rider and the driver profile (POL-GEN-22). No confidence uplift applies, and no profile field may be used to supply a fact about TRP-05019.

ruling.explanation:
Both sides measure this trip the same way, and the record supports it. The platform's trip record shows the recommended route was 11.8 km and the vehicle was actually driven 13.1 km, so the deviation is 1.30 km — 0.30 km beyond the 1.0 km tolerance (POL-RD-22, using trip_record.actual_distance_km and trip_record.optimal_distance_km). The GPS trace is used only to show which route was taken and when, and it shows the vehicle leaving the recommended route at the PIE / Adam Road exit at 17:04:15 and rejoining at Bishan Road / Braddell Road at 17:16:09 — a sustained departure, not a kerbside manoeuvre. The LTA advisory for exactly that segment (PIE, Adam Road to CTE interchange) covers the trip window (16:22:25–17:52:25) and records type NONE: no incident, roadwork or closure, speed bands 4–5 throughout. The reroute was therefore not traffic-justified (POL-RD-23), and the driver's assertion that the PIE was slow cannot supply that justification. That places the case in row (d) of POL-RD-24 — not traffic-justified, deviation over 1 km — which refunds the excess distance fare in full. That fare is the deviation distance times the base per-km rate, without surge: 1.30 km × 0.72 SGD = 0.94 SGD, which is also the figure the fare ledger itself derives. The rider asked for 3.00 SGD; the policy measure is 0.94 SGD, so the rider is owed part of the contested amount and the balance of the charge stands. On the two points the parties argued: whether the driver messaged the rider about the slow PIE, and whether the rider agreed, does not change the outcome, because row (d) contains no notification element at all — the refund follows whether or not notice was given. For the same reason the impaired chat log (EV-CHAT-05019, weight 0.6, issue code TRUNCATED_LOG, only 2 of 4 entries exported and nothing after pickup) is not a carrier of any decisive fact here and does not lower this ruling's confidence; the decisive facts come from the trip record, the LTA advisory and the fare ledger, all complete at weight 1.0. The profiles do not decide anything: the only fraud-related field, fraud_flags, is 0 on both the rider and driver profiles, so no confidence uplift applies (POL-GEN-01, POL-GEN-22). This is a case the AI may finish rather than hand up: the dispute value is 3.00 SGD, below the 10.00 SGD band where an AI ruling is final, no fraud flag is present, the deviation is within the 2 km AI limit, and no safety indicator appears (POL-GEN-22, POL-RD-25). The driver's compensation is nil; the money moved is the rider's 0.94 SGD refund.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
